title: Apple (AAPL) hits a $1 Trillion Market Cap - Can Bitcoin do the same? — Crypto Invest Help
text:
No one has missed the boat in Crytpo, we are all building the boat together. Apple (AAPL) hits a $1 Trillion Market Cap - Can Bitcoin do the same?
Apple ( AAPL ) became the first company in the world to hit the magical $1 trillion market cap number last week, but the road to success has not been linear, and investors had to possess very deep conviction to hold on to those stocks - there were moments in which selling would have looked like the only option, however if you kept those strong hands you would be a very happy investor indeed. Today we are going to take a look at that journey, and draw some parallels with Bitcoin.
First thing is first - Bitcoin never had an IPO, or to use crypto parlance, an ICO. Bitcoin was the brainchild of Satoshi Nakamoto - who may or may not be a single entity, or a group of people. The AAPL IPO was launched on December 12th in 1980. This IPO was the largest since the Ford Motor Company in 1956, raising more than $100 million and instantly created more millionaires (about 300) than any other company in history, with Steve Jobs 11% stake instantly making him worth $130 million. At the time of launch shares were $22.00, but factoring in adjustments, it would be a price of around 39 cents.
If you had purchased $990.00 worth of AAPL at IPO, you would have approximately $521k today. In 2009 when Bitcoin was conceived, the same $990.00 would have got you 183,333 BTC, which would be worth $1.185 billion. Of course, this isn't comparing Apples with Apples! Apple was an established company which had been in operation for 4 years at the time, whereas Bitcoin was a mere concept, and more of a gamble on what could be possible with 'magic internet money'
Whilst Apple was an established company, it was still a risky investment - no one could possibly have known what the personal computer would do to the IT industry. In fact, in 1982, the New York Times cautioned against investing in hyped-up tech companies like Apple.
"Strong performance of a new issue in it's fledgling months, of course, is no guarantee of longevity," the newspaper wrote at the time . “Dozens of offerings from last year are currently outright disasters, and even the most talked about deals of the past two years – Grenetech, Apple Computer, and Cetus – are all trading significantly below their offering prices.”
It's true in the case of Grenetech, a bio-pharmaceutical that collapsed and Cetus, another that was acquired, that these stocks did not have the longevity of AAPL, however, Bitcoin has had it's obituary written many times over (306 in fact!), and seems to come back stronger each time.
As recently as 2002 there was not a single mutual fund that counted AAPL as it's largest holding, however, fast forward to today, and there are now 3577 mutual funds that hold the stock, with a fair portion of those recognising it as their largest.
Apple has had to go through various board room battles and turmoil to get where it is today, and who is to say a cautious investor wouldn't have sold their holdings prior to Steve Jobs taking back the helm in 1997 after his largely failed splinter company NeXT was acquired by the conglomerate.
In fact, there was a general perception in the market around that time that Apple had peaked. The message was that investors needed to face the music, and the Apple story was over.
To understand Apple's success, we need to understand the mindset of the investor. Apple is an emotional stock - people get excited about the capabilities, the design, the product. Apple enthusiasts will line up in the middle of winter outside a store with a sleeping bag, so they can be among the first to get their hands on a new iPhone. The holders of the stock we're never interested in selling on the next big release or riding a wave up until that point - they were betting on Apple's ability to continue to innovate.
Bitcoin investors are the same. Most hard-core Bitcoin maximalists probably couldn't even tell you the price at any given moment or period of time. What they can do is tell you about all the times in history where a population suffered at the hands of a government debasing a currency, or the harm Keynesian models inflict upon an economy. Bitcoin enthusiasts are excited about the capabilities of hardened digital money, the ability to break the shackles of a centralised financial system that continues to create further disparity between the rich and the poor.
It took around 20 years for Apple to exceed $1.00 per share, this was effectively a 2.5x ROI, and then over the last 16 years, the growth has been parabolic. This growth was enabled by the ubiquity of the internet and our digital environment - it is fair to say that Apple have contributed to this environment, contributing to a self fulfilling prophecy.
Bitcoin has been around for approximately nine years - the speculative growth the project has seen is like nothing the financial community has witnessed before. Right now, we are on the cusp of a moment in time where financial institutions like the Intercontinental Exchange , Goldman Sachs and the NASDAQ are exploring the financial applications of the technology.
You may have been lucky enough to buy AAPL at some point in it's first 20 years - if so, congratulations to you if you have held on to that stock through-out that period. It has been proven as one of the most sound financial investments possible. Apple are a business that has gone from strength to strength, and they still have some room to move yet.
If you had $990.00 to invest today, would you be better off investing in Apple? or investing in BTC? That money would get you 4.72 Apple shares, which would probably be worth a tidy sum in another 40 years, or would you be better off investing in 0.15 BTC which you could obtain for the same price? This is a technology in which the full potential is yet to be realised. The sceptics among us may suggest that Bitcoin is going to zero. Apple had to deal with the same attitudes all those years ago, and look how it turned out for them.
Now is your opportunity to invest in something as monumental as Bitcoin which may have the capacity to change the financial system as we know it, within it's first 10 years of existence. Don't end up like Ronald Wayne, the famous 3rd founding member of Apple who sold his shares for $800.00 (worth $100 billion today), dip your toe in the water , and that meagre investment might pay for your kids college tuition.
